transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for students in grades 6 through 8. The draft plan includes two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. Before I can sign off on approval, I'd like to hear from each of you on any relevant considerations. Let's start with you, teacher -- what are your thoughts on the proposed plan?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important staffing issue. Yesterday I received the finalized roster from the activities office, and it contains 18 student tutors. However, the draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two adult supervisors. According to the school's supervision rule, one adult can supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. With 18 tutors, we would need at least three adult supervisors, not two.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. My student-support review, which I completed this week, identified two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so this information wouldn't be visible to anyone else coordinating pairings. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be left to student selection -- they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor to ensure we don't inadvertently violate those no-contact orders.
